description: Insect Study introduces the most numerous animals on Earth: safety around stinging insects, anatomy and orders, life cycles, observing and identifying insects, social insects, their role in ecosystems and agriculture, conservation, and careers or hobbies.

safety.note: Know how to recognize and respond to severe allergic reactions to stings.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Collect insects only where it is legal; collecting is prohibited in many parks and refuges.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Safety
requirements.summary: Hazards from stinging and biting insects and treating stings, including severe allergic reactions.

requirements.title: Anatomy and orders
requirements.summary: How insects differ from other arthropods, and the major insect orders.

requirements.title: Life cycles
requirements.summary: Complete and incomplete metamorphosis, and raising an insect through its life cycle.

requirements.title: Observing insects
requirements.summary: Observing and identifying live insects across several orders and their roles in ecosystems.

requirements.title: Social insects
requirements.summary: One option: observing an ant colony or a beehive.

requirements.title: Insects in ecosystems
requirements.summary: Insects in food webs and as pollinators.

requirements.title: Insects and people
requirements.summary: Bees and colony collapse, and alternatives to insecticides.

requirements.title: Conservation
requirements.summary: An insect migration and a threatened or endangered insect.

requirements.title: Careers or hobbies
requirements.summary: One option: an insect-related career, or a hobby.
